name: narrative-constraint
operation: read structure off the symmetry of rule application — compare how a stated constraint is applied across cases and take the asymmetry as the signal
valid_on: a constraint that was actually stated, plus two or more cases it is claimed to cover, where the cases are comparable and the application is observable
breaks_when: the cases are not comparable, so an asymmetry in application may be a real difference between the cases rather than a selective rule; or the constraint was never stated, so consistency is being measured against a rule the reader supplied. And structurally: it operates on representations, so it cannot separate an inconsistent account from an inconsistent world — a faithful account of an asymmetric situation scores the same as a selective account of a symmetric one.

explore_paths.question: How does constraint consistency relate to trust?
What measurement instruments detect selective application?
How does information entropy reveal rationalization?
